  "outcome_variable": "is_low_score (low_review_score)",
  "per_column": [
    {"name": "summary_length", "causal_role": "other", "named_in_query": false, "rationale": "Generic surface feature of the text; not a candidate cause of low scores nor a common cause of any treatment and the outcome. Descriptive noise."},
    {"name": "text_length", "causal_role": "other", "named_in_query": false, "rationale": "Mechanical length metric with no clear causal relation to satisfaction; not a treatment or confounder."},
    {"name": "has_negative_words", "causal_role": "mediator", "named_in_query": false, "rationale": "Negative wording is an expression of the (dis)satisfaction that also produces the low score; it lies on the path from the underlying experience to the outcome rather than being an exogenous cause. Effectively a proxy/mediator of the outcome, not a confounder."},
    {"name": "has_positive_words", "causal_role": "mediator", "named_in_query": false, "rationale": "Same reasoning: positive wording reflects the same latent sentiment that drives the score. Adjusting for it conflates outcome with predictor."},
    {"name": "helpfulness_ratio", "causal_role": "collider", "named_in_query": false, "rationale": "Helpfulness votes are determined AFTER and partly BY the review content and score; it is a downstream consequence, so conditioning on it risks collider bias, not confounding."},
    {"name": "has_complaint_markers", "causal_role": "mediator", "named_in_query": false, "rationale": "Complaint language is a manifestation of dissatisfaction that co-occurs with the low score; on the causal path from experience to outcome, not a common cause."},
    {"name": "uppercase_ratio", "causal_role": "other", "named_in_query": false, "rationale": "Stylistic emphasis feature; at best a weak proxy of emotional tone (thus mediator-like), not an independent common cause of a treatment and the outcome."},
    {"name": "exclamation_count", "causal_role": "other", "named_in_query": false, "rationale": "Punctuation/emphasis proxy for affect; reflects sentiment rather than causing the score. Not a genuine confounder."},
    {"name": "question_count", "causal_role": "other", "named_in_query": false, "rationale": "Surface punctuation feature; no clear common-cause relationship to any treatment and the outcome."},
    {"name": "is_low_score", "causal_role": "outcome", "named_in_query": true, "rationale": "This is the focus outcome itself, derived from Score; not a covariate."}
  ],
  "treatment_present": false,
  "treatment_columns": [],
  "confounders": [],
  "confounder_quality": 0.0,
  "rationale": "The added columns are mechanical text features (lengths, punctuation counts, uppercase ratio) plus lexical sentiment proxies (has_negative/positive_words, complaint_markers) and one downstream helpfulness measure. None of these is a well-defined TREATMENT whose effect on low scores is being attributed, nor a genuine CONFOUNDER that is a common cause of both a treatment and the outcome. The sentiment/complaint columns are expressions of the same latent (dis)satisfaction that produces the score (mediators/outcome proxies), and helpfulness_ratio is a post-outcome collider. No exogenous common cause (e.g., product quality/category, price, delivery/shipping issue, reviewer harshness, product age) was surfaced. The set fails the causal-estimation test: no treatment identified and no genuine confounders adjusted for."
}
